name: Gremlin Swarm

items.name: Absolute Nuisances
items.text: 5 feet. The gremlin swarm constantly harasses nearby creatures to break their concentration, kicking shins and screaming in ears. A creature in the aura taking a concentrate action, must first succeed at a DC 18 Will save save or lose the action. Creatures occupying the gremlin swarm's space take a –2 circumstance penalty to this save.

items.name: Clever Little Monsters
items.text:
Frequency once per round

---
Effect The gremlin swarm cooperates to harass a foe, attempting to disarm, grapple, shove, or trip a creature that occupies the swarm's space. The swarm can use their Thievery ( disarm skill=thievery, grapple skill=thievery, shove skill=thievery, or trip skill=thievery) modifier, rather than Athletics, for the skill check for this action.

items.name: Grem-a-pult
items.text:
Frequency once per round

---
Effect The gremlin swarm hurls a hapless "volunteer" at the enemy. Each creature in a 5-foot burst within 30 feet takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 21 basic Reflex save save). A creature who critically fails the save is also Clumsy 1 for 1 round. The gremlin swarm then loses 1d4 healing Hit Points as the gremlin scuttles back injured.

items.name: Swarming Blows
items.text: Each enemy in the mob's space takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage (DC 21 basic Reflex save save). A creature that fails this save is also knocked Prone.

text:
Most gremlins are communal creatures, dwelling in gangs, mobs, and hives just out of mortal sight. These groups are often contentious, each gremlin believing they are taking advantage of the rest, yet they never live alone if they can help it.

On occasion, an entire mass of gremlins can be roused to anger. Such a swarm is surprisingly coordinated and effective, driven not by any one gremlin's leadership but by their excellent instincts for causing trouble. Gremlin swarms cooperate easily to bring down much larger foes, trussing them up like a holiday goose or poking them with knives and claws until they stop twitching.

---
Like many fey, gremlins personify a natural force of the world: entropy. It's a fundamental truth that everything breaks, that every complex system, from a machine to a society, will inevitably grind itself down to nothing. Gremlins are happy to give those complex systems a friendly shove down the stairs.

Nearly all gremlins live in the Universe, where they have fully acclimated to the plane. No one is quite certain why, but it seems likely that some long-forgotten gremlin managed to so irritate the Eldest to such a degree that their entire species was exiled—though it appears the Eldest missed a few, as some gremlins still lurk in the First World.

Gremlins are usually found in an odd, parasitic relationship with mortal communities in the Universe. They don't need to eat or sleep, don't age or sicken, and never really die—but they do need to cause trouble. It's as essential to them as food and drink are to mortals, and nowhere do they get as many chances for chaos and confusion as in a mortal settlement. Gremlins thus become pests, living on the margins of society and bedeviling anyone and anything they can get their hands on.
